mostWorthwhile.text: Packaging fat into chylomicrons was most worthwhile: the description explains how intestinal cells rebuild fat and makes the unfamiliar particle name meaningful before its lymph route.

leastWorthwhile.text: The separate glucose and amino-acid crossings felt repetitive. Their picture descriptions show where the molecules go but do not explain how they cross the cells.

surprise.text: The contrast that fat is rebuilt and packaged before entering lymph, rather than following glucose and amino acids directly into villus blood, changed my understanding of the routes.

arbitrary.text: Combining glucose and amino acids already in villus blood felt somewhat artificial as an action, although it usefully showed their shared route toward the liver. The title 'portal blood' was not explicitly explained.

continue.text: I would probably continue to see how the nutrients are used after absorption; the contrasting routes were interesting, though some individual crossings felt repetitive.
